findings.title: fetch_error_details zips error_ids with events.values() which can misalign when events are missing
findings.body: In `fetch_error_details`, `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` returns a dict that may have fewer entries than `node_ids` if some events are not found. The code then does `zip(error_ids, events.values())`, which pairs error_ids positionally with whatever values exist in the dict. If a middle event is missing from nodestore, subsequent error_ids will be paired with the wrong event data. For example, if error_ids=[a,b,c] and only events for a and c exist, the zip produces (a, data_a) and (b, data_c), attributing c's data to b. The fix is to iterate over node_ids and look up each one in the events dict individually, e.g., `for event_id, node_id in zip(error_ids, node_ids): data = events.get(node_id)`.

findings.title: Cross-validation of age/timestamp uses truthiness check, failing when value is 0
findings.body: In `validate_timestamp`, the check `if self.initial_data.get('age')` uses truthiness, meaning an `age` value of 0 (which is valid per the spec — a report generated 0ms ago) would be treated as absent, allowing both `age=0` and `timestamp` to coexist without triggering the mutual exclusion validation. The same issue exists in `validate_age` with `self.initial_data.get('timestamp')` when timestamp is 0. Use `is not None` or check key presence with `'age' in self.initial_data` instead.

findings.title: TableWidgetVisualization rendered with hardcoded empty data when feature flag is enabled
findings.body: When the `use-table-widget-visualization` feature flag is enabled, the code renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />` — always an empty table regardless of the actual `result.data` and `result.meta` available in scope. This means any organization with this feature flag enabled will see blank tables instead of their dashboard data. The actual data from `result.data` and `result.meta` should be passed through.

findings.title: Dead code: _handle_regex_match defined but never used in parametrize_w_experiments
findings.body: After removing `ParameterizationRegexExperiment`, the local function `_handle_regex_match` inside `parametrize_w_experiments` (lines 335-343) is defined but never called. It was previously used in the `else` branch for regex experiments. This is dead code that should be removed to avoid confusion.

findings.title: analytics.record uses request.user.id which may fail for org auth token requests
findings.body: The `analytics.record` call at line 85 accesses `request.user.id` unconditionally. However, this endpoint supports org auth token authentication (checked later at line 137 with `is_org_auth_token_auth(request.auth)`). When authenticated via an org auth token, `request.user` may be an `AnonymousUser` or a special token user that doesn't have a standard `id` attribute, potentially causing an `AttributeError`. The analytics event definition marks `user_id` as `required=False`, so it should be conditionally included only when a real user is present.

findings.title: get_environment_info calls get_recommended_event() for each issue, which may be expensive
findings.body: `get_environment_info` is called for every issue in the PR comment list (up to 5 issues from `get_top_5_issues_by_count`). Each call invokes `issue.get_recommended_event()` which likely performs database queries or snuba queries to find the recommended event. This happens synchronously during PR comment generation, potentially adding significant latency. Consider caching or batching these lookups, or making this information optional with a timeout.

findings.title: age field lacks min_value constraint allowing negative values
findings.body: The `age` field is defined as `serializers.IntegerField(required=False)` without a `min_value` constraint. Per the Reporting API spec, `age` represents milliseconds since the report was generated and should be non-negative. A negative age value would pass validation but is semantically invalid. Add `min_value=0` to match the constraint already applied to `timestamp`.
